proof.criterion: Shutdown waits for every running intake handler before the database pool closes (review thread PRRT_kwDORFy7ds6xSaz8)
proof.surface: The real envoy-dispatch binary, config B (fake GitHub holding a merged pull request's fetch), one idle process, SIGTERM during the hold
proof.command: headproof6 check 1 (dispatch://INFRA-607/artifact/stop-path-proof-md, raw runs stop-path-proof-raw-tar-gz); go test ./cmd/dispatch/ -run TestShutdownWaitsForAnIntakeHandlerBeforeClosingThePool
proof.observed: At 67c3d0f2: the fake answered 3 s after SIGTERM, the delivery_pull_requests row was written and last_event_at set, the message acknowledged (ack floor 1/1), and only then the process deregistered and closed its pool; exit 3.06 s after SIGTERM, no 'closed pool' line. The test passes.
proof.negativeControl: At 4f9bd6e8 the process deregistered 0.6 s after the signal while the handler waited on GitHub, then logged 'process event ... closed pool' and acknowledged the message with no row and a null last_event_at; the test failed on the old order with that output.

proof.criterion: A stop drains the subscription the bus holds after a connection replacement, not the dead original (review thread PRRT_kwDORFy7ds6xSa0G)
proof.surface: The real binary with its intake's NATS connection closed by a TCP proxy's -ERR so the client replaces it and restores the subscription, then SIGTERM while a pull request's fetch is held
proof.command: headproof6 check3.sh and check3b.sh; go test ./internal/dispatch/delivery/ -run TestAStopAfterTheConnectionWasReplacedDrainsTheRestoredSubscription; go test ./internal/bus/ -run TestDrainSubscriptionDrainsTheHandleARestoreBound
proof.observed: At 67c3d0f2: after 'resubscribing' and 'recovery successful', no drain ERROR at SIGTERM; the durable lost its subscriber 15 ms after the signal; a message published after SIGTERM was not delivered to the stopping process; the next process handled the held messages once each and wrote the row.
proof.negativeControl: At 4f9bd6e8: 'drain the intake's subscription error="nats: connection closed"' right after the signal, the subscription stayed bound until the client closed, and the message published after SIGTERM was delivered to the stopping process; the delivery test failed on the old code ('the stopping intake's subscription stayed bound to the durable').

proof.criterion: A handler cut off by the stop deadline hands its message back
proof.surface: The real binary, GitHub holding a fetch 50 s, SIGTERM 2 s after publishing
proof.observed: Exit 15.08 s after SIGTERM with the hand-back line; the message stayed unacknowledged (num_ack_pending 1); a fresh process was redelivered it once and wrote the row.
proof.negativeControl: With GitHub answering at once the process exits in about 0.07 s with no hand-back line (headproof4 and round 3 checks).

proof.criterion: Every changed loop is silent at idle; the remaining timers are named
proof.surface: Two head and two fork-point processes side by side, statements by source over 10 minutes
proof.observed: 4.50 -> 3.34 statements per second per process; embedding scan, coverage, task progress, reference excerpts, suggestion outcomes and edit notices at zero; edit notice sent 10 ms after it fell due with no statement before.
proof.negativeControl: The fork point in the same window ran each changed loop on its timer (edit notices 481 statements, embedding scan 240).

A draining registration is skipped by restoreSubscriptions and subscriptionsHealthy, so a connection replaced during the stop does not re-bind it.
